target_customer: Mexican corner shops (tienditas) and their suppliers
problem: Offline corner shops and their providers struggle with cash flow and access to credit; the company began with point of sale, then inventory-based lending, then AI collection agents for supplier invoices.
business_model: Lending to corner shops against inventory, later fees on AI-driven invoice collection for suppliers
product_category: SMB fintech: inventory-based lending and AI collections (LatAm)

founders.name: Carlos Tejeda
previous_startups: Orca Wireless (wireless internet network serving over 250K customers in Northern Mexico, exited)

founders.name: Oscar Rydberg
founders.background_notes: YC page lists building the GRC intranet system and the ORCA top-up and wireless access system and designing ORCA WiFi access point hardware.

founders.name: Rafael Tejeda Elizondo
education: Instituto Tecnologico y de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, Bachelor of Laws (1992)
University of Texas at Austin McCombs and CIMAV, MS Technology Commercialization (2010)

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer vision on inventory photos to build credit and risk models (about 90 percent accuracy claimed) and a lending stack, built by a very small team.

defensibility.rationale: Repayment and inventory data could compound, but lending needs capital and Mexican SMB lenders were numerous.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought the company as far as found.

market_need_then: The YC launch post cites about 70 billion dollars per year of gross merchandise value in the corner shop segment and 6,000 plus shops served; a 2021 TechCrunch piece states about 86 percent of Mexican payments were cash and many lacked credit.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found; the name resembles a Spanish phrase for ask and shares a stem with Pidedirecto but no source explains it.

pivots.from: Point of sale for corner shops
pivots.why: Access to capital was the shops' biggest problem per the YC page

pivots.to: AI collection agents for corner shop suppliers' invoices
pivots.why: Uses collection and reconciliation tools to win suppliers as customers per the YC page; date not stated

outcome_analysis: Pideaky is active with a very small team and no public priced round, so its funding is unknown rather than zero. It moved from point of sale to inventory lending and then to AI collections for suppliers, and claims over 14,000 loans and 6,000 shops. The founders have long ties to corner shop customers through the payphone business. Whether the latest pivot works is not yet visible.
notes: The company site pideaky.com returned HTTP 503 so only the YC description was available. The YC page says it is backed by Wayfinder and Goodwater with no amounts; CB Insights lists about 130,000 dollars over two rounds, the latest seed dated 2021-08-31, and other trackers list Olive Tree, Dupe Ventures, Leonis and Sprint VC, all aggregator only and unverified so no round is recorded. Competitors: a search found YoFio, Konfio, Fairplay and Pulpos but only in undated or later pages, so the list is empty. The 86 percent cash figure is from a TechCrunch article on Nelo, April 2021, seen only in a search summary. Traction figures are from the company's launch post and unverified. Completeness pass: the 130K seed dated 2021-08-31 rests on databases (CB Insights, Extruct); investor lists differ and CB Insights counts two rounds in total, so another round may be missing.
